title: Protocol for Preparing Fiber-Defined Simulated Media for Growth Profiling of Gut Bacteria
author: Sagam, Aleti

steps.title: Set up anaerobic chamber
steps.instruction: Prepare the anaerobic workstation with a premixed gas mixture of 10 % H₂, 10 % CO₂, and 80 % N₂ and allow O₂ to drop below 1 ppm; set the chamber temperature to 37 °C; place empty sterile bottles, tubes, pipette tips, and heat‑labile reagents (vitamin‑mix, vitamin K stock, hemin stock, lipid stock) inside and let them pre‑reduce for 12 h (up to 16 h).

steps.title: Prepare YCFA basal medium
steps.instruction: Dissolve the YCFA basal components (per 1 L final volume) in deionized water: Casitone 10 g, Yeast Extract 2.5 g, Glucose 5 g, K₂HPO₄ 0.45 g, KH₂PO₄ 0.45 g, NaCl 0.9 g, MgCl₂·6H₂O 0.0375 g, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.09 g, NaHCO₃ 4 g, L‑Cysteine·HCl 1 g; add distilled water to 992.5 mL. Adjust pH to 6.8–7.0, bring to 1 L with water, autoclave at 121 °C for 15–20 min, cool to ~40 °C and aseptically add heat‑labile components: Simplified VFA mix 6.25 mL, Hemin 10 µg/mL (add 125 µL of 80 mg/mL stock), Vitamin K 11 µg/mL (add 100 µL of 10 mg/mL stock), Vitamin mix 1 mL. Transfer the sterilized medium to the anaerobic workstation, loosen caps slightly, and allow it to equilibrate anaerobically for ≥12 h before use.

steps.title: Prepare YCFA agar plates
steps.instruction: Prepare YCFA basal medium as above but add 1.5 % (w/v) agar before autoclaving. Autoclave at 121 °C for 15–20 min, cool to ~50 °C, aseptically add the same heat‑labile components (VFA mix, hemin, vitamin K, vitamin mix). Pour the molten agar into sterile petri dishes inside a biosafety cabinet (or adjacent to the anaerobic workstation), allow plates to solidify completely, then transfer them to the anaerobic workstation for pre‑reduction ≥12 h before streaking.

steps.title: Prepare high‑fiber medium
steps.instruction: Modify the YCFA basal formulation with the high‑fiber components (per 1 L): Yeast Extract 2.5 g, Inulin 10 g, Pectin 3 g, Potato Starch 10 g, plus the same mineral/vitamin salts as the basal medium (K₂HPO₄ 0.45 g, KH₂PO₄ 0.45 g, NaCl 0.9 g, MgCl₂·6H₂O 0.0375 g, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.09 g, NaHCO₃ 4 g, L‑Cysteine·HCl 1 g) and distilled water to 992 mL. Mix thoroughly on a magnetic stir plate for 10–15 min (turbidity is expected). Adjust pH to 6.8–7.0 if needed, autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min, cool to ~40 °C, then aseptically add heat‑labile components: Simplified VFA mix 6.25 mL, Hemin 5 µg/mL (62 µL of 80 mg/mL stock), Vitamin K 11 µg/mL (100 µL of 10 mg/mL stock), Vitamin mix 1 mL. Transfer to the anaerobic workstation, loosen caps, and pre‑reduce for ≥12 h before inoculation.

steps.title: Prepare low‑fiber medium
steps.instruction: Modify the YCFA basal formulation with the low‑fiber components (per 1 L): Yeast Extract 2.5 g, Peptone 10 g, Glucose 10 g, Fructose 10 g, Sucrose 10 g, Tween 80 0.5 % (v/v) (0.5 mL), plus the same mineral/vitamin salts as the basal medium (K₂HPO₄ 0.45 g, KH₂PO₄ 0.45 g, NaCl 0.9 g, MgCl₂·6H₂O 0.0375 g, CaCl₂·2H₂O 0.09 g, NaHCO₃ 4 g, L‑Cysteine·HCl 1 g) and distilled water to 989.1 mL. Mix thoroughly on a magnetic stir plate for 10–15 min. Adjust pH to 6.8–7.0 if needed, autoclave at 121 °C for 15 min, cool to ~40 °C, then aseptically add heat‑labile components: Simplified VFA mix 6.25 mL, Hemin 5 µg/mL (62 µL of 80 mg/mL stock), Vitamin K 11 µg/mL (100 µL of 10 mg/mL stock), Vitamin mix 1 mL, Palmitic acid 0.3 mg/mL (add 3 mL of 100 mg/mL stock, keep warm to prevent precipitation). Transfer to the anaerobic workstation, loosen caps, and pre‑reduce for ≥12 h before inoculation.

steps.title: Store and re‑equilibrate media
steps.instruction: All liquid media (YCFA basal, high‑fiber, low‑fiber) may be stored at 4 °C under aerobic conditions for up to 1 week; before use, re‑introduce them into the anaerobic workstation and allow ≥2 h of re‑equilibration. YCFA agar plates may be stored inside the anaerobic workstation for up to 2 weeks.

description: The protocol below describes preparation of fiber-defined simulated media and comparative growth profiling of human gut bacterial isolates under controlled anaerobic conditions. The basal medium used throughout this protocol is Yeast extract–Casitone–Fatty acid (YCFA) medium, a widely used anaerobic formulation that supports robust growth of phylogenetically diverse gut isolates in vitro. This workflow was developed to evaluate microbial growth dynamics under contrasting substrate environments that model differences in dietary fiber availability. While basal anaerobic media such as YCFA provide nutrients sufficient for general cultivation, they are not specifically configured for structured comparison of growth responses under defined fiber-enriched versus low-fiber conditions. In this protocol, YCFA is adapted to generate fiber-defined simulated media that differ primarily in fiber complexity and carbohydrate composition while maintaining constant buffering capacity, mineral composition, vitamin supplementation, and reducing conditions. Standardized inoculum normalization controlled anaerobic handling, and media-specific optical density blank correction are implemented to ensure reproducible comparison across isolates and dietary conditions. Although optimized for phylogenetically diverse anaerobic gut isolates, this protocol can be adapted to additional obligate or facultative anaerobic species with appropriate adjustment of inoculum density and incubation time.
